title: AlgoTest vs Opstra (2026): Which Options Platform Is Better for Indian Traders?
summary: AlgoTest vs Opstra compared for 2026. See how Opstra DefinEdge login, pricing and features stack up against AlgoTest's backtesting and algo trading.
body_markdown:
AlgoTest and Opstra are two of the most widely used options platforms in India, and traders often shortlist both. They look similar on the surface, but they solve different problems.


Opstra is an options analytics terminal, built for studying implied volatility, open interest and option chain behaviour in depth.[AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=seo&utm_term=algotest&utm_content=main-page) is an end-to-end algo trading platform, built to take a strategy from idea to backtest to live automated execution.


This comparison covers what each does in 2026, what both cost, and which one fits your trading style.


## What Is Opstra DefinEdge?


Opstra, short for Options Strategy Analytics, is an options analysis platform built by Definedge Securities, a broking and trading-tools group based in Pune. You will also see it called Opstra Edge or Opstra DefinEdge, since it sits inside the wider Definedge ecosystem alongside tools like Zone and TradePoint.


It is aimed at traders who want analytical depth rather than a simple order window. Core features include:


-


A strategy builder with payoff charts, Greeks, IV smile and probability of profit for multi-leg positions.


-


Implied volatility analysis covering IV rank, IV percentile and term structure across underlyings.


-


Open interest tracking with build-up and unwinding scans, timestamped intraday.


-


Historical option chain replay, which lets you inspect how the chain looked on any past date.


-


Coverage across the F&O, currency and commodity segments.


Definedge describes Opstra as offering 27 or more analytical features across its free and PRO tiers.


## How to Access Opstra: Login, Free Tier and PRO


Opstra is tied to the Definedge account system, which shapes both how you log in and what you pay.


**Opstra login.** You sign in at the Opstra site using your UCC, password and an OTP, or reach it from your Definedge MyAccount dashboard.


**Do you need a Definedge demat account?** For the free tier, yes. Many traders keep their existing broker and subscribe to Opstra separately for the analytics.


**Free vs PRO.** Open interest tracking across strikes is usable without paying. IV analysis, backtesting, scans and historical chain replay all sit behind the PRO subscription.


**The detail most comparisons miss.** PRO subscription amounts convert into wallet points you can offset against Definedge brokerage. If you trade actively through Definedge, the effective cost drops substantially. Through any other broker, you pay full price.


## What Is AlgoTest?


AlgoTest is a no-code[algo trading software](https://algotest.in/blog/10-best-algo-trading-software-in-india-2025) for Indian retail traders. Build a strategy, backtest it, forward test it with virtual capital, then deploy it live through your broker, all in one place. It is web-based and works through the browser across devices.


-


A drag-and-drop[strategy builder](https://algotest.in/blog/option-strategy-builder-algotest/) with leg-wise settings, entry and exit timing controls and re-entry rules on stop-loss.


-


[Backtesting](https://algotest.in/feature/backtest) across Nifty, Bank Nifty, Finnifty, Midcap Nifty, Sensex and Bankex, with roughly 7.5 years of data and portfolio-level testing.


-


[Paper trading](https://algotest.in/paper-trading) to validate a strategy in live conditions before committing capital.


-


Live algo execution with broker integrations, M2M tracking and indicator-based automation.


-


An[Option Simulator](https://algotest.in/blog/opstra-simulator-vs-algotest-option-simulator/) that replays past trading days so you can practise entries, exits and adjustments.


-


Signals AI, which turns a plain-English strategy description into something you can backtest and deploy.


-


TradingView, Chartink, PineScript and custom-code integration for signal-driven automation.


-


A built-in[F&O margin calculator](https://algotest.in/blog/margin-calculator-by-algotest) for sizing positions before you place them.

## Where Opstra Is Genuinely Strong


Opstra earns its reputation in three areas:


-


**Volatility analytics.** IV rank, IV percentile and term structure across underlyings go deeper than most Indian platforms offer.


-


**Open interest scanning.** Build-up and unwinding scans with intraday timestamps show clearly where positioning is shifting through the session.


-


**Historical chain replay.** Pulling up any past date and inspecting the chain as it stood is genuinely useful when studying how an expiry behaved.


If you already hold a Definedge demat account, the wallet-points arrangement also makes PRO far cheaper than the list price suggests.


Related:[AlgoTest vs Sensibull: Feature Comparison (2026)](https://algotest.in/blog/algotest-vs-sensibull/)


## Where AlgoTest Pulls Ahead


The gap opens the moment you move from analysis to execution.


-


**Automated deployment.** Opstra helps you decide what to trade. AlgoTest runs it for you, so a tested strategy executes without you placing each leg by hand.


-


**Broker flexibility.** Opstra's execution is tied to the Definedge ecosystem. AlgoTest integrates with multiple brokers, so you keep your existing demat account.


-


**Intraday backtest depth.** Opstra's free-tier backtesting is largely end-of-day, a real constraint for intraday options. AlgoTest runs on intraday data across several years, with 25 free backtests every Monday. Our guide on[how to backtest options strategies](https://algotest.in/blog/how-to-backtest-options-trading-strategies-with-examples/) walks through the process.


-


**A connected workflow.** The strategy you build carries through to backtesting, paper trading and live deployment without being rebuilt in another tool.


-


**Indicator-based automation.** TradingView, Chartink and PineScript signals can drive live orders. Opstra does not target this workflow.


-


**Portfolio-level testing.** Comparing several strategies side-by-side shows whether your book is diversified or just running the same risk four times.


## Pricing: AlgoTest vs Opstra


The charging models differ more than the headline numbers. Opstra sells a subscription window. AlgoTest sells credits you spend only on what you use, and unused credits stay in your account.


### Opstra pricing


-


PRO costs Rs 1,300 per month plus 18% GST.


-


A 6-month PRO plan works out to roughly Rs 1,000 per month plus GST, a discount of around 23%.


-


The basic tier is free for Definedge demat account holders, and PRO amounts convert into wallet points against brokerage.


### AlgoTest pricing


-


Credit packs run from Starter at Rs 499 for 500 credits up to Premier at Rs 5,999 for 7,500 credits, with Explorer and Pro in between.


-


Backtesting costs 1 credit per backtest, plus 25 free backtests every Monday that do not roll over.


-


Live algo execution costs 100 credits per strategy per 28-day cycle, charged pro-rata so it gets cheaper later in the cycle.


-


Forward testing costs 50 credits per strategy per 28-day cycle, also pro-rata.


Full details are on the[AlgoTest pricing documentation](https://docs.algotest.in/getting-started/buy-plan/) .


In practice, a trader who backtests occasionally spends very little on AlgoTest, because a quiet month costs almost nothing. On a subscription, a quiet month costs the same as a busy one. A trader running several automated strategies daily spends more, but is paying for live execution Opstra does not provide at all.


Read more:[StockMock vs Opstra vs AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/blog/stockmock-vs-opstra/)


## Which Platform Should You Choose?


**Choose Opstra if:**


-


Volatility analysis drives your decisions and you want IV rank, percentile and term structure in depth.


-


You already hold a Definedge demat account.


-


You trade discretionary positional options and want research depth rather than automation.


**Choose AlgoTest if:**


-


You want to automate strategies rather than place every leg by hand.


-


You trade through a broker other than Definedge and do not want to switch.


-


You backtest intraday options strategies and need intraday data.


-


You want one platform covering build, backtest, paper trade and live deployment.


Plenty of traders use both: Opstra for volatility research, AlgoTest for testing and automating what that research suggests.

## Getting More From Your Options Strategies in 2026


The choice comes down to whether you want to analyse trades or run them. Opstra's depth in volatility and open interest research is real, but it stops where execution begins, and ideas that stay in analysis mode rarely reach consistent execution.


[AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/) covers the step after research. Build a strategy without code, backtest it on years of intraday data, paper trade it until you trust it, then deploy it live through your existing broker.


Every account gets 25 free backtests each Monday, so you can[start with a free backtest on AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/register?utm_source=blogs&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=seo&utm_source=blogs&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=seo) before spending anything.
